method:
Read-only audit; nothing in the repo was written. Inputs: v2.71 = reference/Cartalith v2.71 DCC test.html (sha256 9e8b78d806f4...), v2.72 = html/Cartalith v2.72 DCC test.html (sha256 003e89b8505c..., identical to commit 7bd3b49 and to HEAD, re-checked at the end). Both were measured from byte copies in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Cartalith-GDT/9bb82d91-f6d5-50c4-b743-a54d60b8e9ff/scratchpad/audit-perf/. html/...v2.73 has since moved on (stage 2 is in progress), so every line number below is v2.72's.

Harness: I set up my own copy of Cartalith_RC's harness at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Cartalith-GDT/9bb82d91-f6d5-50c4-b743-a54d60b8e9ff/scratchpad/audit-perf/rc. Running `node tests/perf/hash_gen1.js v2.71 v2.72` printed ALL IDENTICAL (5 configs, R32F on both sides). So engine and render timings should match between versions, and only shell work can differ. I did not run run.sh or run_um.sh because nothing changed.

Environment: Playwright headless shell chromium-1243, 1400x900 viewport, DPR 1, WebGL2 through SwiftShader (GPU R32F path active), 4-CPU VM. The worker pool engages from 1024 (its threshold is 262144 cells).

A/B design: every comparison ran in separate processes, one fresh browser per sample, versions interleaved ABBA. Samples per version: n=5-7 for load, generate, interaction and shell; n=3-4 for the LOD gesture and the 1024 sliders. Results are medians with [min..max]. I call a difference "established" only when the two ranges do not overlap. The load benchmark was re-run independently twice before concluding, because its first run suggested +7.8% and that did not reproduce.

World setup follows the probe_shellui.js pattern: state.tect.seed=12345, state.resW, _setupSkipped=true, GW=state.resW, GH=gridH(GW), allocate(), await generate(), then _setupHide(). Settlements come from _civIterativeAutoWorld(3), which gives 43 places and 68 ways at 1024.

What was measured and how:
- Main-thread cost: CDP Performance.getMetrics deltas (TaskDuration, ScriptDuration, RecalcStyle and Layout durations and counts, JSHeapUsedSize, Nodes, JSEventListeners).
- Long tasks: a PerformanceObserver('longtask', buffered) installed with addInitScript, plus a rAF interval logger.
- Per-event handler cost: synchronous in-page dispatch timed with performance.now().
- Attribution: CDP CPU profiles (0.1-1 ms sampling), timing-only wrappers on global functions, and switching parts off with measurement-only monkeypatches in the page.

Measurement trap: work run directly inside DevTools' Runtime.callFunctionOn is invisible to the longtask observer and to ScriptDuration (a 4.4 s generate showed 0 long tasks). So generate() was run inside a setTimeout task. Even then ScriptDuration stayed near zero for the 1024/2048 generates, so wall time and long tasks are used for generate instead.

Shared machine: another agent shares it (load average 0.6-5.7 during the session, and another Chromium was running during the last two runs). Absolute milliseconds are indicative only; ratios and attributions are what count. Load average is logged per sample in the JSONL.

Scripts are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Cartalith-GDT/9bb82d91-f6d5-50c4-b743-a54d60b8e9ff/scratchpad/audit-perf/scripts/: bench.js (modes load, gen, interact), shell.js, slider.js, split_event.js, wheel_attr.js, prof_gen.js, routing_dupes.js, prof_lodwheel.js, lod_ctrl.js, profile_load2.js, bootrender.js, prof_domain.js, listeners.js, trace_idle.js, geom.js, sun_probe.js, civtime.js, summarize.py, driver.sh, driver2.sh. Raw data is in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Cartalith-GDT/9bb82d91-f6d5-50c4-b743-a54d60b8e9ff/scratchpad/audit-perf/results/.

Summary: v2.72 adds no measurable cost on any hot path. Its established regressions are about +11 ms per resize across the 860 px line, +2 ms of style recalc on a desktop resize, and ~34 ms of boot work. The large costs are older, shared by both versions, ranked below. No difference was established for:
- generate at 512, 1024 and 2048
- view-change and slider renders
- wheel and pan handler cost and smoothness
- the File menu (6.8 vs 7.2 ms per click)
- domain switch (48.6 vs 46.2 ms)
- Find (13.1 vs 14.2 ms per key)
- the ResizeObserver refit (1.6 vs 1.4 ms)
- idle cost
- listener growth (none in either version)
- load DCL.

findings.title: v2.72 regression (shell): crossing the 860 px line costs +11 ms main thread per resize (+22%)
findings.evidence:
Measured with shell.js: real CDP setViewportSize 1400<->800, 6 resizes per sample, n=5 per version, interleaved ABBA.
- TaskDuration per resize: 52.8 [46.8..57.6] ms in v2.71, 64.2 [62.9..72.2] ms in v2.72. The ranges are disjoint.
- RecalcStyleDuration 13.0 -> 18.3 ms; LayoutDuration 9.0 -> 13.9 ms; ScriptDuration 6.0 -> 8.5 ms; LayoutCount 9.3 -> 12.8 per resize.
- _dskPlace, timed by a wrapper on the global: 14.4 [11.1..17.7] ms on the first crossing, when it creates the 26 comment markers. Later crossings take 2.9-5.8 ms.
- The interact batch agrees: resize-to-frame 51.6 -> 74.8 ms, LayoutCount over 6 resizes 57 -> 81.

Related: a resize that stays on the desktop side (1400<->1200) costs RecalcStyleDuration 1.38 [1.14..1.51] -> 3.34 [2.64..3.46] ms (disjoint). Its TaskDuration of 16.2 -> 20.7 ms is not established (ranges overlap).

Code: _dskPlace (19356-19373) moves 26 elements with one appendChild each, then calls _syncChromeTop() (19092, two getBoundingClientRect reads, which force a full layout) and _scheduleViewportRefit(). The header ResizeObserver (19121-19122) calls _syncChromeTop again after the same layout change.
findings.proposal:
Remove the _syncChromeTop() call from _dskPlace. The header ResizeObserver at 19121 already republishes --chrome-top and --canvas-top once layout settles. Alternatively, run it inside the rAF that _scheduleViewportRefit already queues. Optionally, append each slot's elements through one DocumentFragment.

Expected gain: one forced layout fewer per crossing, estimated at 3-5 ms. This is not measured. A crossing is rare (window resize or rotation), so it is also acceptable to leave this as is.
findings.risk: Shell only; no engine or render path is touched, so hash_gen1 is unaffected. --canvas-top caps the Layers popover, so after the change, re-run probe_desktopshell.js (174 assertions) and probe_shellui.js on both sides of the line.

findings.title: v2.72 (shell, boot): _dskInit adds about 34 ms of boot work, mostly one extra full layout; no load-time difference is established
findings.evidence:
CPU profile from profile_load2.js, sampled every 100 us, n=5 per version:
- _dskInit: 34 [29..36] ms inclusive, of which _dskPlace takes 31 [26..33] ms.
- _syncChromeTop: 37 [32..40] ms in v2.72 vs 6 [6..10] ms in v2.71. It is the same function, but in v2.72 it forces the first layout after 26 nodes have moved.

DCL across three independent interleaved runs (n=7, 7 and 5 per version):
- run 1: 2496 -> 2690 ms (x1.078), ranges [2274..2891] vs [2566..2928]
- run 2: 2428 -> 2447 ms (x1.008), ranges [2203..2666] vs [2302..2770]
- run 3: 2584 -> 2761 ms (x1.069), ranges [2517..3117] vs [2515..2930]
Every bracket overlaps, so no load difference is established. Two of the three medians are higher for v2.72; the attributed v2.72-only cost is about 34 ms.

Static growth at load:
- elements 2075 -> 2264 (+189, +9%)
- all nodes 5101 -> 5685; CDP Nodes 6471 -> 7056
- JS listeners 544 -> 576
- CSS rules 451 -> 463
- LayoutCount 10 -> 13; RecalcStyleCount 15 -> 18
- with a populated 1024 world: 2526 -> 2715 elements

No listener or node growth over repeated use. listeners.js ran 3 extra rounds of generate, Settings, Settlements, timeline strip, every menu, select/deselect and Find: JSEventListeners stayed 574 -> 574 (v2.71) and 606 -> 606 (v2.72).
findings.proposal:
Place the controls before the boot's first forced layout. Two ways:
- call _dskPlace() before the boot `_syncChromeTop();` at 19124, keeping _dskReady gating (it is a var, so it is hoisted);
- or skip _syncChromeTop inside _dskPlace's boot call and let 19124 run after it.
Either way the page is laid out once, in its final arrangement. Expected gain: about 30 ms off the load long task (estimate).
findings.risk: Shell only; hash-safe. The boot order must respect v2.72's TDZ rule (block-2 lets are read through _dskV) and the _dskReady gate. Verify with probe_desktopshell.js and with a load at phone width.

findings.title: v2.72 (layout consequence, not code): the LOD zoom gesture costs about 10% more at 1400x900 because the map is 30 px shorter
findings.evidence:
Controlled A/B with lod_ctrl.js: a synthetic 40-tick LOD wheel gesture with the settle-refine switched off, n=4 per version.
- Main-thread time: 13.0 [12.6..13.4] s in v2.71, 14.4 [13.9..14.8] s in v2.72 (disjoint).
- Overview rebuilds per gesture: 31 -> 32.

Map viewport size (.canvas-wrap, from geom.js): 684x792 in v2.71 vs 684x762 in v2.72 at 1400x900. At 1920x1080 it is 1152x972 vs 1152x942. The difference is the timeline strip sitting above the status bar in every domain.

Cause test: with v2.71's window shortened to 870 px, its wrap is also 684x762. Then both versions do 32 rebuilds, and main-thread time is 13.2 [13.1..14.9] s vs 13.8 [13.4..15.7] s (overlapping). That run had another agent's Chromium on the machine.

The earlier real-input A/B (n=3) also read v2.72 as worse (long tasks 14.5 -> 21.7 s). But its settle-refine count varied from 0 to 10 per run (a timer race), so it cannot separate the versions.
findings.proposal: No v2.72-specific action. The LOD overview-rebuild fix (finding P2-lod-overview-rebuild) removes the per-tick cost in both versions. Worth recording: LOD cost depends on the viewport's aspect ratio, so any band that changes the map's height shifts it.
findings.risk: None. This finding is informational, and it prevents a false regression claim.

findings.title: Engine, both versions: generate() at the default 2048 grid takes 68 s and freezes the page in one 60 s task; 62% of it is buildRoutingSurface, and half of those builds repeat an identical one
findings.evidence:
Generate A/B (bench.js gen, n=5 per version):
- 2048: 68.4 [65.3..70.5] s vs 67.7 [65.4..70.4] s.
- Longest single task at 2048: 60.5 [58.0..62.8] s vs 60.5 [58.4..62.7] s. The busy overlay cannot repaint during it, so it shows no progress and input is ignored.
- 1024: 16.5 s, with a 13.9-14.0 s longest task. 512: 4.8 s as a single task.
- Stage medians at 2048: carveRivers 30.9-32.5 s; render 11.4-11.6 s (prologue 8.5-8.7 s, pixels 2.6-2.7 s); flow1 7.8-7.9 s; flow2 7.7-8.3 s.

Profile of one 2048 generate (prof_gen.js, timing wrappers on globals):
- buildRoutingSurface ran 6 times: 7.1, 7.8, 7.1, 7.1, 6.7 and 6.8 s, totalling 42.5 s of 69.1 s.
- computeFlow ran 4 times for 33.3 s; each call is about 85% routing surface (radix sort 0.6 s, accumulation about 0.5 s).
- Self time: MinHeap.pop 26.0 s, buildRoutingSurface 6.1 s, MinHeap.push 1.5 s.

Duplicate builds (routing_dupes.js, seeds 12345 and 31337, at 512 and 1024): every generate builds the surface 6 times. Three of those builds take a byte-identical input (FNV of the field bytes, plus sea level, world flag and size) to the build before. All three duplicates also produced byte-identical output (0 mismatches in 12 pairs). They cost 466-813 ms of 1145-1520 ms per generate. The three duplicates are:
- flow2 repeats flow1 (refreshClimate does not touch the field);
- carve's buildRiverNetwork, through currentRoutingSurface(), repeats carve's computeFlow;
- renderNow's prologue repeats carve's final computeFlow.

Cause in code:
- computeFlow (6765) bumps _fieldGen, then calls buildRoutingSurface(field, ...) directly (6775).
- currentRoutingSurface (6759-6764) caches on _fieldGen only, so it always misses after a computeFlow. Its key also omits seaLevel and world, although both are inputs of buildRoutingSurface.
- buildRoutingSurface (6720-6752) pushes every sub-sea cell into its heap. Measured: 95.7-98.1% of those are interior ocean (all 8 neighbours sub-sea), which can close nothing when popped. That is 41-59% of all cells in the four worlds tested.
findings.proposal:
(A) Use one content-keyed routing-surface cache in both computeFlow and currentRoutingSurface. Reuse the stored surface when GW, GH, seaLevel and world match and `field` is bitwise equal to a stored copy (compare as Uint32Array views: about 3-5 ms at 2048, plus 11 MB of memory). Same input gives the same output, as measured above. Expected gain: 3 of the 6 builds disappear, about -21 s of the 68 s at 2048 (-31%); the render that ends generate drops from about 11.5 s to about 4.7 s.

(B) Seed the priority flood only with sub-sea cells that touch a non-sub-sea neighbour or a map edge: mark interior cells closed, but do not push them. The heap then starts with 2-4% of the ocean instead of all of it, which means far fewer pops and a heap that fits in cache. Expected gain (estimate): most of the remaining ~21 s.

(C) On the pool path, yield to a macrotask between the post-pool stages and set the busy label per stage. The page then shows progress instead of freezing for a minute.
findings.risk:
ENGINE: hash_gen1 must print ALL IDENTICAL before and after.

(A) is identical by construction. But adding seaLevel and world to the key changes when the surface rebuilds after a sea-level change (today it silently reuses the surface built for the old sea level). Measure the sea slider after making this change.

(B) only reorders equal-priority pops. The output should not change: each cell takes max(own, closer+EPS) from its first popped neighbour, and pops are monotone. That is an argument, not a proof. Prove it with: hash_gen1 --full; a byte-compare of buildRoutingSurface's output, old against new, over several seeds, region and world extents, and three sea levels; tests/run.sh (1280/0) and run_um.sh (882/0).

(C) must keep the no-pool headless path synchronous: the v0.61/v0.135 contract is that the suite calls generate() without awaiting it. A yield also lets dock handlers (sliders, Generate) run mid-generate, so add an input guard while _busyDepth>0.

findings.title: LOD render, both versions: wheel-zooming in (auto-LOD past 2.2x, the default) blocks the main thread for about 13-15 s per 40-tick gesture, with one ~0.4 s overview rebuild per tick
findings.evidence:
Single run with prof_lodwheel.js: real CDP wheel input, 20 ticks in and 20 out at 1024 with settlements, v2.72.
- 15.3 s of wall time; 37 long tasks totalling 13.4 s, mostly 300-650 ms each.
- p95 frame interval 450 ms.

Real-input A/B (n=3 per version): v2.71 long tasks total 14.5 s [13.3..18.8], p95 frame interval 467 ms.

Controlled A/B (lod_ctrl.js, n=4 per version): 13.0 s and 14.4 s of main-thread time, 31-32 overview rebuilds per 40 ticks. The wheel handler itself takes 0.2 ms.

CPU profile: the setTimeout(0) closure in _lodScheduleOverviewRebuild (14210-14232, closure at 14215) accounts for 12.5 s of 15.3 s. Inside it, renderBiomeTileRGBA takes 9.0 s and amplifyRegion 3.7 s.

Its own comment (14197-14209) says the overview is rebuilt 'in the background'. But setTimeout(0) runs on the main thread right after each tick, and the v0.93 estimate quoted there (100-130 ms per rebuild) measures 300-650 ms here. The stretch-streak cap (LOD_OV_STRETCH_STREAK_CAP=4, line 14352) also forces a synchronous rebuild every 5th consecutive stretch.
findings.proposal:
Debounce the deferred rebuild until the gesture settles, for example 150 ms after the last view change (like scheduleLodRefine's 240 ms), and keep stretching the last overview in the meantime. Replace the 4-frame streak cap with a time-or-ratio cap, so a continuous gesture does not force synchronous rebuilds. Later, move the overview into GENPOOL: amplifyRegion is already in the worker source, and the colorization would have to be added.

Expected gain (estimate): 1-3 rebuilds per gesture instead of 31-32, so main-thread time per gesture drops from about 13-15 s to about 1-2 s.
findings.risk: LOD render only. hash_gen1 renders off-LOD and is unaffected, and the LOD pixels at rest stay identical (same functions, same inputs). smoke_gen1.js pins the current overview and streak behaviour (the v0.93 hotfix tests, about lines 2362-2426), so those tests must be updated deliberately. A longer stretch shows as a transient blur during the gesture, which a person needs to look at: the owner reported 'blocky' LOD in v0.92 and v0.93.

findings.title: Render, both versions: dragging any look slider re-renders the whole map on every input (2.6-4.3 s per step at 2048, 0.7-1.0 s at 1024)
findings.evidence:
slider.js sends 8 'input' events per slider, one every two frames.

At 1024 (n=3 per version), render per input, v2.71 / v2.72:
- exag 737 / 721 ms
- bioBlend 681 / 690 ms
- aoR 768 / 766 ms
- sea 1004 / 1043 ms (longest task 1.2-1.3 s)
- peak 740 / 700 ms, plus a 23-26 ms handler
There is no version difference.

At 2048 (v2.72, one run), render per input:
- exag 2971 ms; bioBlend 2633 ms; aoR 2998 ms
- sea 4259 ms (longest task 5.8 s)
- peak 2656 ms, plus a 111 ms handler
The peak handler is slow because its 'input' handler (17589) runs recomputeClimate() synchronously, without rAF coalescing.

36 of the 57 top-level bind() sliders call render() on 'input' (command: grep -n "^bind('" FILE | grep -c "render()"). Each input changes _civBakeKey (21911), so the bake cache misses and a full renderNow (10730) runs: the pixel loop, plus a getImageData read-back of the whole map (16 ms at 2048).
findings.proposal:
1. Drag preview: on 'input', render at stride 2 or 4 (compute every 2nd pixel and draw it scaled); render exactly on 'change'. Never store a preview in _civBakeCache.
2. Move recomputeClimate out of the peak slider's 'input' handler into rAF or 'change'.
3. Longer term, split the pixel loop across the GENPOOL workers. They run the same JS, so the arithmetic stays identical; the fields would be shipped once per _fieldGen/_climGen.

Expected gain (estimate): stride 2 means about 4x fewer pixels, so about 0.7-1 s per step at 2048; the workers would give about 3x more.
findings.risk: RENDER: the exact render (what hash_gen1 hashes) must stay byte-identical. The preview must never be cached, exported, or baked into the atlas or LOD caches. A low-resolution preview is visible during a drag, which is the owner's call.

findings.title: Shell/boot, both versions: every page load spends about 1.9 s rendering an empty 2048x1311 ocean behind the 86%-opaque setup gate
findings.evidence:
Unprofiled boot render (bootrender.js, n=5 per version): PERF.render.total of the boot renderNow is 1846 [1770..2149] ms in v2.71 and 1960 [1838..1999] ms in v2.72.
- prologue about 1.03 s: water bodies, the routing surface of an all-ocean field, sea shading;
- pixels about 0.75 s;
- overlays about 0.1 s.
It sits inside a load long task of 2.13 / 2.31 s. DCL is 2.4-2.8 s and FCP about 0.25 s, so the gate card is painted early, but its buttons cannot respond for about 2 s.

CPU profile (n=5): the boot renderNow is about 90% of script block 1. GPU.init (shader compiles and self-tests) adds 156-159 ms to the same task.

Code: 20199-20202 runs `else { renderNow(); ... _setupOpen('intro'); }`. #onboard's background is rgba(10,12,17,.86). I looked at the screenshot /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Cartalith-GDT/9bb82d91-f6d5-50c4-b743-a54d60b8e9ff/scratchpad/audit-perf/shots/boot_v272.png: it shows a faint, vignetted dark-blue ocean behind the card.
findings.risk: Shell/boot. hash_gen1 is unaffected, because it generates before hashing. Leave the headless branch (typeof indexedDB==='undefined') untouched so tests/run.sh stays at 1280/0. The RC probes that open the page all generate before reading the canvas (checked by grepping tests/perf for _setupOpen and #onboard). The gate's backdrop becomes a flat colour instead of a faint ocean, which a person should look at.

findings.title: Engine/civ, both versions: auto-populating settlements blocks the page for 15-16 s; 85% of that is one Dijkstra per settlement that evaluates a Tobler edge cost on every relaxation
findings.evidence:
bench.js interact at 1024 (n=5 per version): _civIterativeAutoWorld(3) takes 15.3 [14.3..16.8] s in v2.71 and 15.9 [14.7..16.1] s in v2.72, producing 43 places and 68 ways.

Profile at 512 (civtime.js; 17.3 s total):
- _civHierarchicalNetwork accounts for 14.3 s. It runs one full-grid roadDijkstra per settlement: res1 and res2 are `rp.map(ri => roadDijkstra(cost, ..., eg))` at 28398 and 28427. roadDijkstra totals 15.0 s inclusive.
- The edge-cost closure built by _civLandTimeEdgeCost (27681, closure at 27685) takes 9.8 s inclusive.
- Inside it, toblerKmh takes 4.5 s self (two Math.exp per edge, through _civSlopeTimeK), and _civGrade 0.9 s.
- The heap's pop takes 1.6 s.
findings.proposal:
Build an 8-direction edge-cost table once per cost grid: a Float64Array of RW x RH x 8 holding exactly what the closure returns (about 6 MB at the 384-px routing grid). Pass a table lookup as edgeCost to every roadDijkstra of that build.

Expected gain (estimate): about 8-9 s of the 15-17 s.
findings.risk: ENGINE/civ. hash_gen1 does not see the civ layer, so verify separately: an FNV hash of JSON(state.places, civWays) before and after, over several seeds and both extents, plus probe_roadconnect, probe_foodshed and probe_trade. The table is only valid if the cost, delay and river inputs do not change between the searches of one build. Reading 28388-28427, the discounts are applied before eg1 and eg2 are built, but re-check before relying on it.

findings.title: Render layer, both versions: off-LOD wheel zoom reallocates and redraws the settlement canvas at a new zoom-dependent size on every tick (25 ms median, 67 ms p90 per tick at 1024)
findings.evidence:
bench.js interact at 1024 with settlements (n=5 per version):
- Synthetic wheel-tick handler: median 22.2 / 22.6 ms, max 64-68 ms; 18 civ canvas reallocations per 24 ticks.
- Real CDP wheel input, 40 ticks: p95 frame interval 117 ms in both versions; 17 long tasks totalling 1.64 s, the longest about 164 ms.
- Middle-drag pan is fine: 1-3 ms per move.

Cause test (wheel_attr.js, v2.72, 72 ticks per variant):
| variant | median | p90 |
|---|---|---|
| as shipped | 24.6 ms | 67.1 ms |
| civ redraw off | 0.4 ms | 0.4 ms |
| civ canvas held at its zoom-1 size, still redrawn each tick | 2.0 ms | 2.8 ms |
| scale bar off | 36.9 ms | 61.5 ms (no gain) |

At the 4096 cap, resize plus draw takes 9 ms against 1 ms for the draw alone. At 2048 a zoomAt in/out pair takes 15.8 ms.

Code: applyView (18378-18394) calls drawCivLayerAuto, which calls _civSyncCanvas (20891-20900). That sizes civCanvas to cssW x dpr x viewT.scale (capped at 4096) and resets it whenever the size moves by more than 2 px, which is every tick.

The 2 forced layouts per tick (updateScaleBar's read after the transform write, and _civSyncCanvas's clientWidth after the scale bar's innerHTML) are real but measured negligible: about 0.2 ms of layout per tick. Fixing them first would gain nothing.
findings.proposal:
During a gesture, keep the civ canvas at its current backing size and let CSS scale it; resize and redraw once when the zoom settles (debounce about 150 ms). Alternatively, quantize the zoom used for sizing to steps (1, root 2, 2, 2 root 2, 4), so a full zoom-in reallocates only a handful of times. For wheel and pan input, coalesce applyView's civ redraw to one per frame.

Expected gain: per-tick cost from about 25 to about 2 ms median and from about 67 to about 3 ms p90 (measured with the canvas held). The p95 frame interval should approach 33 ms (not measured).
findings.risk: Civ layer only. hash_gen1 hashes the terrain canvas (vctx), not civCanvas, so it is unaffected. Labels and pins look softer while zooming until the settle redraw, which a person should look at. Keep direct drawCivLayerAuto() calls synchronous: smoke_gen1.js reads civ canvas pixels right after them (about lines 263, 2652 and 2812).

findings.title: Render cache, both versions (correctness and visuals): the Sun direction slider does nothing, because the bake-cache key reads state.sun, which does not exist
findings.evidence:
Code: _civBakeKey (21911-21921) builds its key with `state.sun`, but the state literal (3427) and bind('sun', ...) (17617) use `state.sunAz`.

sun_probe.js, 512 world, both versions: moving #sun from 315 to 45 degrees
- leaves the key unchanged;
- runs no pixel loop;
- leaves the map hash unchanged.
After _civBakeCache.clear(), the map does change, so the render does depend on the azimuth. A positive control (the exag slider) changes the map. Of the probe's 3 assertions, 1 fails on both v2.71 and v2.72, and that failure is the bug.

slider.js agrees: renderMs for sun is 0 at both 1024 and 2048.
findings.proposal: Replace `state.sun` with `state.sunAz` in _civBakeKey, and add sun_probe.js to RC tests/perf: it fails today and should pass after the fix. This is the same class of bug as v0.70's seaLevel and v0.86's _climGen key fixes, so check every part of the key against the state literal.
findings.risk: Render cache key only; no pixel arithmetic changes. hash_gen1 does not move sunAz, so it stays ALL IDENTICAL. Once fixed, dragging the slider costs a full render per step (see P3-slider-full-render).

findings.title: Shell, both versions: every domain switch resets the user's zoom and pan, and redraws the settlement layer twice (about 46-49 ms per click)
findings.evidence:
prof_domain.js: after zooming to 2.07x (v2.71) or 1.99x (v2.72), every switch between World, Civil, Carto and Explore returned the view to the cover scale (1.151 / 1.105).

Cause: _applyDomainUI ends with an unconditional _scheduleViewportRefit() (18062). Its _refitViewportNow (19110-19115) calls _viewFill() (18313: pan 0, scale = cover), even when .canvas-wrap did not change size. The ResizeObserver at 19117-19123 already covers real size changes.

shell.js (real clicks, n=5 per version): 48.6 / 46.2 ms of main thread per switch, about 30 ms of it script. The profile shows 2 drawCivLayer per switch, one via _civSetTool and one via the refit.
findings.proposal:
Drop the unconditional _scheduleViewportRefit() at 18062 and rely on the ResizeObserver. Alternatively, have _refitViewportNow clamp with _viewClampFill instead of re-filling when the box is unchanged.

Expected gain: the zoom survives domain switches, and each switch does one civ redraw fewer (estimate 5-15 ms).
findings.risk: Shell. This changes behaviour (zoom is kept across domains), which is the owner's call. The conditional bands that v2.24 added the refit for must still refit through the observer: check probe_domainrail and probe_desktopshell.

findings.title: Civ render layer, both versions: the territory brush rebuilds the whole territory raster on every pointermove (23 ms per step at 2048)
findings.evidence:
split_event.js: one _civPaintTerritoryAt step costs 6.5-7.7 ms at 1024 (both versions) and 23 ms at 2048 (v2.72).

Code: each step bumps _civTerrGen (21954-21965), so drawCivLayer (21393-21430) rebuilds the full GW x GH ImageData (a loop over every cell, then putImageData) and redraws the layer.
findings.proposal:
Write only the brush's bounding box into the scratch ImageData (putImageData with a dirty rectangle), and keep the full rebuild for every other key change.

Expected gain (estimate): per-step cost proportional to the brush area, a few ms at any grid size.
findings.risk: Civ layer only; hash_gen1 is unaffected. After a stroke, the territory raster must be byte-identical to a full rebuild: compare the two once in a test.

findings.title: Smaller costs, both versions: per-render readout scan, bake-cache read-back and size, Find index, 3D idle loop (no leaks, and no idle work in 2D)
findings.evidence:
From split_event.js:
- updateReadout costs 4.3-4.8 ms at 1024 and 16.3 ms at 2048 on every full render; maxGrade alone measured 18.8 ms at 2048 in a separate run. It scans tempField and makes maxGrade's pass over the field.
- The bake cache reads back the whole map with getImageData after every cache-miss render: 3.5-4.1 ms at 1024, 16.2 ms at 2048. That is on a software canvas here; on a GPU canvas it is a GPU read-back.

CIV_BAKE_CACHE_MAX (21910) keeps 6 full-map ImageData whatever the grid size. That is 6 x GW x GH x 4 bytes: 64 MB at 2048x1311, about 258 MB at 4096, about 1 GB at 8192. These are computed, not measured.

Find costs 13.1 / 14.2 ms of main thread per keystroke in both versions, because it rebuilds the control index each time (_findRun, 17431).

3D view: _v3dLoop (20067) re-requests a frame every frame while 3D is on, even when nothing is dirty. Code only; WebGL cannot be measured here.

Idle and leaks:
- trace_idle.js recorded 0.3-0.8 ms of main-thread work in 3 s of idle, in both versions.
- listeners.js found no listener or node growth.
findings.proposal:
- Cache maxGrade and the temperature range by _fieldGen/_climGen.
- Bound the bake cache by bytes (for example 128 MB) instead of by entry count.
- Build Find's control index once per focus of the search box.
- Stop _v3dLoop when nothing is dirty; _v3dKick already restarts it.
findings.risk: Shell and render tail; hash-safe, because none of these touches pixel arithmetic. A byte bound on the bake cache changes only its hit rate.

limits:
What a headless run here cannot show (needs a person):
- SwiftShader emulates WebGL/GPU paths and canvas compositing on the CPU. Real-GPU timings need a person: a 4096-px civ canvas, a GPU getImageData read-back, the 3D view, worker-pool behaviour in other browsers, and real touch and pinch. touchmove calls applyView per event, the same civ-resize path as P6-wheel-civ-canvas-resize.

Not measured:
- High-frequency trackpad wheel input.
- Phone and tablet layouts: stage 1 changes the desktop only. Desktop was measured at 1400 px wide, with geometry also at 1100 and 1920.
- Export and atlas baking.
- 4K and 8K grids: the bake-cache sizes there are computed, not measured.

Sample sizes:
- Engine A/B used one seed (12345). Duplicate routing builds were confirmed on two seeds at 512 and 1024.
- The 2048 generate attribution is one profiled run; its stage totals match the 5-sample A/B medians.
- Single-run figures: prof_gen, split_event at 2048, the 2048 sliders, prof_lodwheel, prof_domain. Every A/B figure is n >= 3 per version.
- Expected gains are estimates from measured parts unless stated as measured. Nothing was changed, so no fix was measured end to end.

Observation for the visuals pass: a 1100-px desktop window leaves the map 384 px wide in both versions (geom.js). That is a layout point, not a performance finding.

Text for the main loop (I did not edit MISTAKES.md):
- Candidate entry, 'Write or extend a cache key': check every part against the state it names. _civBakeKey reads state.sun, which does not exist (the slider writes state.sunAz), so the Sun slider serves a stale image in v2.71 and v2.72. Verify with sun_probe.js.
- Candidate entry, 'Defer work to "the background"': setTimeout(0) is still the main thread. _lodScheduleOverviewRebuild's comment says the overview rebuilds in the background, but it runs right after every wheel tick: 31-32 rebuilds, about 13 s per 40-tick gesture at 1024.

Suggested backlog rows for OUTSTANDING_WORK.md: P1-generate-routing-surface (A then B), P2-lod-overview-rebuild, P3-slider-full-render, P4-boot-render-behind-gate and P7-sun-slider-bake-key. Each touches engine or render output, so each must re-run hash_gen1 ALL IDENTICAL, tests/run.sh 1280/0 and run_um.sh 882/0 before it lands.
